@graph.scopeNote: The single moment the four records Lane_0 wrote become reachable by reference rather than just present on disk: Task_Link is what a knowledge-graph reference in a paper, an L2 or an L3 artefact actually resolves through, and until it runs, dublin-core.jsonld and its siblings are files in library/ that nothing in the graph points to yet.

@graph.label: Corpus — L1 source knowledge graph
@graph.scopeNote: Whichever branch Gateway_Gates takes, this lane is where the outcome lands, and it is never silence: Task_Declare and Task_StayRef are the process's only two ends, both bean-noted, because a node with no recorded state is invalid rather than defaulted. A refusal is written down with the same weight as a success — the graph still knows the node exists either way.

@graph.label: Corpus — L1 source knowledge graph
@graph.scopeNote: Where the refreshed content actually lands, and the one place the five import gates are re-asked rather than inherited — a licence can change since the original import, and a collection can grow past a size somebody already agreed to, so passing the gates once is never treated as passing them for good.

@graph.label: Corpus — L1 source knowledge graph
@graph.scopeNote: Every path ends here with something written down. A refused sample stays referenced with the refusing gate's reason, a failed import records what failed, and a passed one records where it landed. None ends in silence, because an import nobody can tell was tried is the one somebody tries again.

@graph.definition: Trusted registries and observatories outside this instance's control. Carries no skills because nothing here instructs it.

@graph.label: Trusted registries and observatories (external)
@graph.scopeNote: Task_VerifyAuthority and its gateway sit here rather than with Lane_Agent because the decision is not this instance's call — it is a readout of what the external API returns, and the moment that answer is uncertain or absent, Lane_WorkPlan opens a bean rather than this lane inventing a verdict.

@graph.label: Portal (external consumer)
@graph.scopeNote: The only lane outside this instance's control, so P_Verify checks against an external trust anchor — the GDHCN trustlist — rather than against anything the pipeline itself asserts. When that trustlist cannot be reached, this lane's answer is `unknown`, and GW_Verified routes it the same way as a mismatch: to the last good version, never to a guessed pass.

@graph.definition: The agent activity log. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: it is written to at task start and task end, and emptied by an actor — one entry, all of them, or on a periodic sweep — and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan` and `corpus`, the two existing stores that are acted upon rather than acting. Its entries are held in the instance's unpublished store and never reach a published graph; the `activity-log` skill names the location, which is deliberately not repeated here because a role description IS published.

A session's context — who is acting, which instances are open, what it waits on. A MECHANICAL role and an `actedUpon` one: written to as the session moves and read by a sibling deciding whether a claim is live, and it decides nothing. Modelled on `work-plan`, `corpus` and `log`, the stores that are acted upon rather than acting. It carries `session-context` because the shape of what is written IS the discipline here — unlike `work-plan`, whose store has a CLI, this one is written by a machine that may be an LLM playing the part, so the schema is the contract.
The authoring agent in the editorial lane: auditing a block's prose, structure and sourcing rather than writing new subject matter.
The authoring agent producing what a person reads ABOUT the instance — generated references, the glossary, sticky notes, theme art and deployment documentation.
The authoring agent working on how this instance PUBLISHES itself — the MCP projection, its contract, and the rendering endpoints.
The authoring agent managing the SESSION rather than the content: what this session intends, what is already in flight elsewhere, and what to pick up next.
Watches the default branch and open branches for newly-landed work that an existing audit axis should be re-run over. Reports findings; does not author the fix.
Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.
Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.
Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.
